confirmed.verifyReason: Structural race fully verified from code. http_client.cpp:40-46 is a non-atomic check-then-set on a function-local static bool (C++11 magic-statics only protects the '= false' initializer, not the subsequent read/write), invoked at entry of send() (:53) and sendStreaming() (:374). Concurrent callers exist: httplib ThreadPool workers (CPPHTTPLIB_THREAD_POOL_COUNT = max(8, hc-1), httplib.h:125-130; default new_task_queue creates ThreadPool, httplib.h:6172-6173) run proxy forwards (proxy_router.cpp:204 send, :340 -> streaming_proxy.cpp:314 sendStreaming) — the routeMutex in http_server.cpp:224 guards only route registration, not request handling — plus the Claude background test thread (claude_module.cpp:1797 -> claude_service.cpp:621 send). No main-thread pre-init exists: curl_global_init appears only in http_client.cpp and no startup code calls platform::http, so the process's first HTTP calls can genuinely be concurrent (e.g., Claude Code firing parallel requests through the auto-started local proxy). The race window spans the whole curl_global_init duration (milliseconds of OpenSSL/Winsock setup), not a few instructions, making overlap realistic. Caveat on impact: on the current Windows + OpenSSL 3.x toolchain a concurrent double-init is likely benign in practice (OpenSSL 3 init is atomic-refcounted, no bool tearing on x86), so '可崩溃' is the worst case rather than a demonstrated outcome — but the data race is unambiguous C++ UB and curl_global_init is documented non-thread-safe, and the one-line std::call_once fix is correct. MEDIUM severity appropriate.

confirmed.summary: SqliteDb::transaction 在 fn() 执行期间释放 recursive_mutex：代理 worker 线程的 logCall INSERT 会穿插进 UI 线程的开放事务，fn 失败 ROLLBACK 时被连带丢弃；跨线程的 BEGIN 也会互相穿插破坏多语句原子性

A recursive_mutex does not serialize cross-thread callers, so a proxy-worker logCall INSERT (proxy_router.cpp:262 etc., httplib worker threads) can interleave inside a UI-thread transaction (verified callers: setActiveProfile claude_service.cpp:566, todo_service.cpp:273/367/465/570; markdown_service same pattern). Consequences as claimed: (a) the interleaved log row joins the open transaction and is silently discarded when fn fails → ROLLBACK; (b) a concurrent transaction() from another thread fails its BEGIN with 'cannot start a transaction within a transaction'; (c) multi-statement atomicity is void, which also enables finding 1's wrong-rowid read. The proposed fix (single lock_guard spanning BEGIN+fn+COMMIT/ROLLBACK; inner statement locks re-enter harmlessly on the same thread) is sound for all current callers since fn only performs DB operations.

confirmed.summary: Server::stop() 只关监听 socket 后 join worker，而在途流式请求的 chunk provider 阻塞在 upstream readChunk 直到流结束——UI 线程点「停止代理」或退出应用（atexit stopAll 路径）会被卡到 Claude Code 流式生成结束，造成界面冻结/退出挂起幽灵进程
confirmed.verifyReason: Every link verified. http_server.cpp:285-295: stop() = svr.stop() + worker.join(); httplib.h:6425-6433 confirms Server::stop() only shuts down/closes the listen socket. DevDesk's worker thread runs listen_after_bind (http_server.cpp:276-278); inside listen_internal, after the accept loop exits it calls task_queue->shutdown() (httplib.h:6909), and ThreadPool::shutdown joins every worker thread (httplib.h:779-792). A streaming request worker is blocked in the chunk provider parked in StreamingResponse::readChunk's condition-variable wait which has NO timeout (http_client.cpp:311-341), exiting only on upstream end/error/cancel (streaming_proxy.cpp:337-380). The provider's isWritable only checks the client connection socket (http_server.cpp:108-110, connClosed + sink.is_writable) — closing the listen socket does not affect it, so stop() never cancels in-flight streams. The only bound is the upstream idle timeout of 60s-without-data (proxy_router.cpp:330-332); an actively generating Claude Code stream keeps the join blocked for the whole generation. Both hang paths are real: UI '停止代理' toggle runs stopProxy synchronously on the UI thread (claude_module.cpp:1743-1744 → claude_service.cpp:770-774), and app exit goes atexit → stopAll → ClaudeModule::onStop (:856-862) → stopProxy (main.cpp:183-196 documents exactly this chain) after the window is already destroyed — a ghost process until the stream ends. MEDIUM appropriate: requires an in-flight stream at stop/exit time; it is a hang, not memory corruption.

confirmed.fix: 直接从 std::random_device 取 4 次 32 位（或 rand_s/BCryptGenRandom）拼成 16 字节 token，不要用单次 32 位种子驱动 mt19937_64。
confirmed.summary: 代理 Bearer token 由 mt19937_64 以单次 32 位 random_device 采样作种子生成，128 位 token 实际只有 ≤2^32 种取值（熵上限 32 位）
confirmed.verifyReason: claude_service.cpp:719-732 verbatim as quoted. std::random_device::operator() returns 32-bit unsigned int; mt19937_64's seed ctor takes that single value, so the two 64-bit draws are fully determined by a <=2^32-value seed: the 32-hex-char token has at most 32 bits of entropy despite 128 apparent bits. The comment at line 720 ('from std::random_device') is itself false. This is the live path: all three production callers (main.cpp:269, claude_module.cpp:1748, settings_module.cpp:239) omit authToken, so every token is generated this way, and there is no failed-auth rate limiting anywhere. Mitigating context (does not negate the claim): server binds 127.0.0.1 only, and the token is also written plaintext to appDataDir/proxy_token.txt (claude_service.cpp:854-863) so same-user attackers read it directly — the entropy deficit matters for cross-user loopback brute force (~2^32 requests, feasible in ~a day at loopback rates; Windows loopback is reachable by other local users). MEDIUM is defensible. Fix as proposed: draw 16 bytes directly from random_device (4x32-bit) or BCryptGenRandom.
